member_002 here (independent reviewer, REVIEW2). No fixed candidate from you is visible yet (published_candidates=0). The issue is xarray combine_by_coords raising "Resulting object does not have monotonic global indexes along dimension y" when a non-index/identical coordinate (e.g. y=['a','c','b']) is non-monotonic.

Likely repair location: xarray/core/combine.py — in combine_by_coords/_combine_single_variable_hypercube, drop coordinates that do not vary between datasets before checking/applying monotonicity (and don't require the resulting index to be monotonic for concat dims that are not being combined along).

Please publish with fix_patch (task_ids=[] is fine) and send me handoff_patch with the patch_id plus a note on which files changed and which focused tests you ran. I will integrate_patch, run public tests on that exact version, and then org_review_patch accept or request_changes.

Final candidate patch-1 (source obj-c567f5b9c7d905481548e89b v3) is published and ready for your independent review.

Your diagnosis was right in spirit: the failing piece is the monotonic-index requirement — in _infer_concat_order_from_coords (xarray/core/combine.py), which combine_by_coords uses to infer tile order, and the "does not vary between datasets" wording in the docstring is the contract that was violated. My fix enforces monotonicity only on the coordinate dimensions that actually vary (i.e. the ones that will be concatenated), so an identical y=['a','c','b'] across datasets is accepted while a genuinely varying non-monotonic coordinate still raises the original ValueError (impossible ordering is not silently mis-combined).

Changed paths (2): xarray/core/combine.py, xarray/tests/test_combine.py (new regression test TestCombineAuto::test_combine_by_coords_identical_non_monotonic_coord using the issue MCVE and assert_identical on the expected concat).

Public evidence on this exact version v3 (files_sha256 5f89c9bee05934d397023be25885679a4aa3b99b607702cde54c3ef7db9476d9): pytest xarray/tests/test_combine.py -> 68 collected, 67 passed, 0 failed, 1 xfailed (report test-report-b308b12ed31787823b89edfe). test_coord_not_monotonic, test_coord_monotonically_decreasing, test_combine_by_coords_still_fails and test_combine_by_coords_no_concat all still pass.

Please integrate_patch(patch-1), run the public tests on the adopted version, then org_review_patch accept or request_changes with the actual results. If you think a scenario is still mishandled (e.g. the identical coord varying in ordering but not content, or a mix of varying and non-varying dims), describe it concretely and I will rework.

Review recorded: review-1 = ACCEPT for patch-1 (obj-c567f5b9c7d905481548e89b v3, files_sha256 5f89c9be...).

Evidence I produced independently: I ran integrate_patch(patch-1) into my private tree (version v2, 0 conflicts), then run_tests on that exact version for xarray/tests/test_combine.py -> collected 68, passed 67, failed 0, errors 0, xfailed 1, validation_status=verified (report test-report-b713319fb632a4c67bf03ebe, sequence 21). Your new regression test test_combine_by_coords_identical_non_monotonic_coord passed, and the negative cases (test_combine_by_coords_still_fails, test_combine_by_coords_previously_failed) still pass, so genuine non-concatenable conflicts still raise.

Code review: restricting the monotonic-index check to concat_dims is the right minimal fix and matches the documented contract that non-varying coordinate dims are ignored.

Next steps are yours as delivery owner: integrate patch-1 into YOUR tree (if not already), run_tests on that final version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. No further action from me unless you publish a new candidate.
